candidates.why: A controlled Gomoku dissection of three self-evolving agents with rule-based ground truth, exact McNemar, and causal interventions shows all three pass the usual proxy signals yet break at different properties; the P(pass)=P(legal)*P(pass|legal) audit is immediately reusable.
candidates.caveat: One game, one base model, one evolution run per mechanism, and no code release, so the drift and override findings are single observations of stochastic processes.

candidates.why: Pre-registered and cleanly isolated, but the frozen strict-order criterion was unsatisfiable by construction (S0 identical to S- in 100/100 pairs), domain A is underpowered, and the proposer is a 0.49B model.
candidates.caveat: The headline that verifier strength does not buy discovery quality generalizes far beyond a 0.49B proposer and two simulated domains.

candidates.why: The FER framing and theory are useful, but the empirical case rests on degenerate untuned SGM baselines, a steep undocumented beta/epsilon ridge, an LLM allocator within noise, and theory assumptions violated by the experiments.
candidates.caveat: SGM-B never accepts a single update, so the state-of-the-art statistical-gate comparison effectively reduces to PACE alone.

candidates.why: A 291-repo census plus a causally isolated gate-patching experiment (34-order gradient drop) and ULP-level verification that FP32 clipping silently zeroes whole batches; three-seed CPT and an oracle baseline support a three-line fix.
candidates.caveat: The 52.6% tying split is confounded by model family and training recipe, and there is no Transformer CPT control for the architecture-conditional claim.

candidates.why: Good control framing and six-seed pretraining, but the main continual-pretraining comparison is single-seed, the gain over ALF-LB is small, and the paper under-weights a real forgetting cost.
candidates.caveat: At alpha 0.8/4 Aux-loss reaches postMV 0.60/0.23, better than PID's 0.90, so the main table is not a matched-balance comparison.

candidates.why: The forward-equivalence reframing is clean and the 95M result is large, but there is one seed, no random-subspace or norm-matched control, and the strongest recent async baselines are not run.
candidates.caveat: Deep pipelines are emulated as P/8 virtual stages on one 8-GPU node with gloo, so the wall-clock conclusions may not transfer to multi-node NCCL deployments.

candidates.why: A pre-registered 17-config sweep across three student-teacher pairs puts quantization, staleness and weight noise on one nats/token scale, brackets an OPD mismatch budget, and localizes 93-99% of FP8-KV damage to layer one with an 8/8 admission check.
candidates.caveat: One main 7B pair for 200 steps, no run inside the budget bracket, and the RL comparison uses baselines that never learned.

candidates.why: Strong theory and impressive fixed-point predictions, but one model (Qwen3.5-9B/LoRA), no RLVR benchmark, and the most quotable K=2 result depends on a reward-specific baseline predictor.
candidates.caveat: GlobalOpinionQA is a 4-5-way single-token task, the easiest possible case for the collapse prediction.

candidates.why: The entropy decomposition is useful, but the headline retention claim spans 83.7-99.9% (the top end is noise), the pass@64 correlation is near-ceiling with n=5-6, and there is no prospective validation.
candidates.caveat: Single seed, LoRA-only, and the q99 stratum captures about 58-59% of GTPO tokens, so that row is not comparable to the others.

candidates.why: The replay and single-coordinate causal trace are excellent, but the paper omits the deterministic Split-K baseline it claims to beat, reports no error bars, and evaluates only 4B-and-under models on one GPU.
candidates.caveat: The 1.02-2.62% overhead is a point estimate plausibly within trial noise, and all seven Civil Comments decision flips are exact 0.5 ties.

candidates.why: Reframes batch invariance as kernel-selection invariance, passes a 26-cell battery on two engines and two GPU generations at 1.08-1.11x stock latency, and shows 512/512 bit-exact rollouts with trainer KL exactly 0.
candidates.caveat: The GRPO stability result is a single-seed sanity test with a lowered learning rate, accuracy is only measured on saturated GSM8K, and there is no released artifact.

candidates.why: A useful taxonomy and case catalog, but the title-keyword sampling is correlated with the symptom being measured, the aggregate is 52% two libraries, and there is no symptom-by-root-cause cross-tab.
candidates.caveat: 47 of 82 deployment failures come from bitsandbytes alone, so the pre-execution-dominates finding is substantially one project's packaging problem.

candidates.why: Pre-registered exhaustive enumeration over the full repair space in three real runtimes shows typical-input gates release 41% of hidden-wrong repairs while one release-note edge input cuts it to 6.5%, replicated across four model families and a blind writer.
candidates.caveat: The 0.410 headline is menu-dependent (0.406 to 0.271 when the menu grows), and 16.8% of the hard distractors still pass the edge-input gate.

candidates.why: A genuinely new threat class with a strong controlled text-swap experiment, but the 64% attack success rate rests on one document per scenario, the chat judge is a vendor under evaluation, and the render oracle is circular.
candidates.caveat: Five documents carry the end-to-end evaluation, so per-system rankings such as 24% versus 22% are uninterpretable.

candidates.why: The arm ladder and oracle-manifest control are well designed, but 91.7 of the 60.4-point headline comes from a by-construction HMAC cell, the confirmatory base is one 8B model, and the gpt-oss replication reverses the thesis.
candidates.caveat: 39.6% benign abstention means the system completes fewer than half of ordinary tasks, a cost the paper never reports as a single number.

candidates.why: Sixty-year paired double-precision controls and a staged ablation chain show float32 drift is an increment-bias problem, not a state-precision problem; the compensated update restores SST RMS to the DP control at 8% or less cost and 1.35x speedup.
candidates.caveat: Fidelity is established only at nominal 1 degree, the residual salinity gain is mechanistically unexplained, and the coupled-model test is underpowered by its own 54 ZJ twin spread.

candidates.why: Careful paired fp16/fp32 verification across five models, but it is an engineering characterization on one year, one GPU and five variables, with a deliberately naive 8-bit baseline.
candidates.caveat: The no-loss-of-skill baseline is each model's own fp32 run against ERA5, which is also the training target for all five models.

candidates.why: Broad simulation study with good HWA/AFM comparisons, but everything is AIHWKit simulation, the main ViT/LLM sweeps are single-seed, and attention stays digital with no system-level energy or latency number.
candidates.caveat: The unmodified-array claim needs a per-array reference column on ReRAM and a per-layer probe readout on PCM, and there is no silicon or code.

candidates.why: Preregistered and well-controlled, but the localization axis is saturated at 72-100%, the 93% headline is a 14-case cell, and the steerability metric rewards indiscriminate damage.
candidates.caveat: Phi's equally well-localized circuit is never causally established; its targeted ablation does not beat random layer sets.

candidates.why: A complete, causally verified ICL circuit across three model families: slot K/V split, 90-reader population, scalar gate, 24 brake heads, matched random controls, a closed-form read law, a gain bound, and released code.
candidates.caveat: The completeness percentage is reference-dependent and moved 0.77 nats after a control fix, and circuit-only beating intact is a metric artifact.

candidates.why: The four-verdict framework and ownership test are valuable, but the shape family is nested and prior-tuned toward ribbon, ownership covers only 46 of 108 concepts, and Tier A's held-out condition is not held out.
candidates.caveat: The 0.1 prior-variance scale on the ribbon cross-features is never swept and may be doing most of the work behind the ribbon result.

candidates.why: Complete TP+SP and MoE training-kernel coverage with 480 microbenchmark cells all faster, one-change-at-a-time ablations isolating queue ordering from self-scheduling, and a free lower-error bitwise-reproducible reduction.
candidates.caveat: Single-node 8-GPU evaluation, proxy-scale 405B (24 of 126 layers), no convergence curves, and no released code.

candidates.why: A real systems insight and 54/54 faster measured points, but there is no partition-size sweep and no overlap-on/off ablation, so the 1.19x cannot be attributed to partitioning.
candidates.caveat: The largest H20 numbers are measured against the authors' own SM90 port of a design that has no public Hopper release.

candidates.why: Correct diagnosis and careful causal index maintenance, but baselines omit the obvious IndexCache combination, accuracy gains concentrate on RULER, and decode is slower than HiSA.
candidates.caveat: No code release, and throughput is single-stream with one server launch per method.

candidates.why: A rare real-incident dose-response study with a striking flat behavior curve, but there are no confidence intervals, the judge is from the same model family, the taxonomy was induced from Mythos 5's own outputs, and no scenarios or transcripts are released.
candidates.caveat: Evaluation awareness rises from 2% to 96.3% across models, so the cross-model table may measure test-taking rather than alignment.

candidates.why: A large, genuinely open model family, but the headline AraIFBench gain is partly training-test verifier coupling, the base model is missing from every main table, and the largest agentic benchmark is unreleased.
candidates.caveat: The 375B is worse than its own 32B on Arabic file processing (64.1 versus 71.8) and AraIFBench, and the report never explains why.
